en.title: Territories without states: mobility, collective labour and inequality in hunting-and-gathering societies
en.deck: Global comparison of mobile and settled foragers, resource rights, reciprocity, stored food and political authority, from Ju/'hoansi networks to the Northwest Coast, Natufian Levant, Jōmon and Poverty Point.
en.regime: Foraging societies combined flexible mobility, negotiated territory, gift networks, resource storage and, in specific cases, hereditary hierarchy without a single universally necessary state or farming transition.
en.key_risk: Treating all foragers as timeless egalitarian bands, or projecting modern ethnographic gift rates and colonial categories backward as direct Paleolithic statistics.

pt-BR.title: Territórios sem Estados: mobilidade, trabalho coletivo e desigualdade nas sociedades caçadoras-coletoras
pt-BR.deck: Comparação mundial entre comunidades coletoras móveis e sedentárias, direitos territoriais, reciprocidade, armazenamento e autoridade, das redes Ju/'hoansi à costa noroeste, Levante natufiense, Jōmon e Poverty Point.
pt-BR.regime: Sociedades coletoras combinaram mobilidade, direitos territoriais negociados, trocas de presentes, estoques e, em casos específicos, hierarquias hereditárias sem exigência universal de Estado ou agricultura.
pt-BR.key_risk: Tratar todos os coletores como bandos igualitários atemporais ou projetar estatísticas etnográficas modernas e categorias coloniais como dados paleolíticos diretos.

contrary_evidence: The ethnographic sample of 32 forager societies is not a census of Paleolithic populations or a universal residential size.
Ju/'hoansi gifting ratios measure different observed gifts and people in 1974 and 2018 and cannot establish prehistoric rates.
Resource concentration has evidence as a mechanism of hierarchy in Northwest Coast/California comparisons, but not a universal causal law for all fishermen.
Poverty Point demonstrates monumental coordination by foragers, not a verified king, tax ministry or hereditary elite.
Natufian intensive wild cereal gathering and possible cultivation are not proof of fully domesticated crops across all communities.
Current Australian cultural fire and Country practices document varied governance and historical continuity, not a continent-wide unchanged regime since the Pleistocene.
limitations: Historical and ethnographic examples span different periods and cannot be merged into a synchronous prehistoric world model.
Modern ethnography is conditioned by colonial relations, land dispossession, fencing, markets and national policies.
Archaeological visibility of rank, household rights and social ties is unequal and does not directly measure global prehistoric income inequality.
The charts concern measured modern 1974–2018 Ju/'hoansi gifting; they are not Pleistocene quantitative reconstructions.
Sources combine full research articles, abstracts and institutional summaries; full independent academic peer review has not been conducted.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: 2 November 2026 BRT; bibliography covers 2004–2026 academic archaeology, anthropology and Indigenous governance; contemporary Ju/'hoansi observations refer to 1974 and 2018.
producer_checks.editorial_novelty: Distinct from the first Paleolithic survival article; institution-centered comparative analysis of access, movement, exclusion, social reciprocity, class formation, settlement intensity and collective engineering.
producer_checks.visual_signature: Both locales carry two numerical charts with matched measured Ju/'hoansi gift percentages [23,1] and [35,45] for 1974/2018, plus two detailed evidence tables, one three-chain causal diagram and one eight-case regional map.
producer_checks.source_check: 22 matching URLs in EN/PT-BR across PNAS, Science, Nature, Annual Review, university archives, UNESCO and HRAF, covering territoriality, exchanges, political hierarchy, Jōmon, Natufian and Poverty Point.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 18 corresponding substantive chapters plus sources, identical 22 URL references and two chart series, same scenarios, cases, evidence, chronology and qualifications.
producer_checks.research_depth: English approx. 4,622 substantive words / 37,324 characters; PT-BR approx. 4,895 substantive words / 40,008 characters, both above the 8,000-character line requirement.
producer_checks.methodology: Comparative archaeological and ethnographic political economy; explicitly differentiate time, region, ancient/modern, evidence/inference, food stocks, access rights and reproducible 1974/2018 cross-sectional survey data.
